newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY-Attitude change produces new-look Umaga.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY-Attitude change produces new-look Umaga.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Jan 10 - Any resemblance between 1997 Wellington Hurricanes Super 12 rugby winger Tana Umaga and the 1996 Wellington Lions fullback of the same name is just that.
The name is the same, but the attitude and work habits are not. The joker in Umaga has not completely disappeared yet, it just appears at the appropriate times, NZPA reports.
The new-look model was on display at the Hurricanes' Super 12 fitness testing weekend in Palmerston North, and his improvement was the talking point of the weekend.
Umaga had looked in the mirror after his disappointing NPC, and he didn't like what he saw.
He was too big and too slow, and unwilling to work hard enough. His All Black chances were rapidly disappearing and the way he was going, he risked sliding into the background.
He did something about it. Umaga hired a personal trainer and now trains six days a week -- against the one day-and-a-bit days' average of the past years.
He's shed 8kg; he's looking for work, and he's right in there duelling with the best of them in the sprint and endurance tests.
Umaga set personal bests in all sprints, strength and endurance tests in Palmerston North.
"I just had a look at myself and figured I was carrying too much weight," said Umaga.
"I just didn't feel 100 percent after the NPC. I was a bit disappointed in what happened as well, so I took it upon myself to get into shape and try to make this year a good one."
Umaga said he had seen his All Blacks ambitions disappearing.
"What's held me back has been my fitness, which has never really been great at all, because I'm not a great trainer.
"Last year I'd train once or twice a week. Since the NPC I've been training four times a week with my trainer and spend the other two days in the gym ... I've really decided to give it a go."
